items.title: The crusade turns on Zara
items.text: The Fourth Crusade cannot pay Venice for its ships and takes Christian Zara for the Venetians in November 1202. The road to Constantinople is open.
items.fits: Leads into the Latin Empire of 1204.

items.title: Genghis Khan
items.text: At a great assembly on the Onon in 1206 Temujin is proclaimed Genghis Khan. Within twenty years the steppe rides west and south.
items.fits: Before the Mongol cards of 1240 and 1241.

items.title: The crusade against the Cathars
items.text: The Albigensian Crusade sacks Beziers on 22 July 1209. Southern France learns what a crusade at home means, and the Church learns how to hunt heresy by inquiry.
items.fits: Fits the heretical end times card of 1206.

items.title: The Golden Bull of Sicily
items.text: In September 1212 Frederick II confirms Bohemia as a hereditary kingdom under the Premyslids, with Moravia as its margraviate. The valley answers to a king in Prague, a margrave and, at night, to whoever holds Kranzfels.
items.ref: Real history (Golden Bull of Sicily, 26 September 1212).
items.fits: Same year as the Frankfurt crowning on the book card; this is the Bohemian side of it.

items.title: Rabbat in the fall of Zhongdu
items.text: Genghis Khan takes the Jin capital Zhongdu in 1215. Rabbat, already old, lives through the killing and is carried off as a Mongol captive.
items.ref: Kindred Most Wanted p. 20 (the captivity); the fall of Zhongdu, 1215, is real history; the year is a house reading.
items.fits: The book places it in the Mongol sweep through the Chin Empire in the early 13th century.

items.title: Magna Carta and the Lateran Council
items.text: King John seals Magna Carta on 15 June 1215; in November the Fourth Lateran Council sets rules for confession and for Jews and heretics across Christendom.

items.title: Bukhara and Samarkand
items.text: The Mongols take Bukhara and Samarkand in 1220. The cities of Khwarazm are emptied, and the dead of Central Asia flood the Shadowlands.

items.title: Jerusalem by treaty
items.text: Frederick II gets Jerusalem back by treaty in February 1229, without a battle. Gabriel Chavez, the Eyes of Alamut among the city's Cainites, watches the Franks return.
items.ref: Real history (Treaty of Jaffa, 1229); Gabriel Chavez from Jerusalem by Night (Dark Ages) p. 62; the year is a house reading.
items.fits: Same year as Camilla and Cretheus in Rome.

items.title: Envoys from the west
items.text: Ventrue of the Empire send envoys east to learn who holds the Moravian march. The Tzimisce of the hills receive them coldly and send them home with gifts that are also warnings.
items.fits: Fits the Holy Roman Empire in 1230 cards; no clan war is started.

items.title: The Mongol summer
items.text: In the spring and summer of 1241 Mongol riders cross Moravia, burning villages and failing before walled places. The valley's families hide their own, and their Kindred, in the hills and the mine.
items.fits: Matches the book card on the Mongol invasion breaking eastern Tzimisce holdings; Moravia is raided, not held.

items.title: The hill sept fights the riders' spirits
items.text: The Garou of the Moravian hills meet the spirits riding with the Mongol host. They hold their caern but lose half their number, and their Kinfolk among the old families grow fewer.
items.fits: The Shadow Lords' backing of the Tatar Yoke is in Russia; this sept fights it at the western edge.

items.title: Mohi and the burning of Pest
items.text: The Mongols beat the Hungarian army at Mohi on 11 April 1241 and burn Pest. Vencel Rikard's plan to make Buda-Pest the greatest city of the region goes up with it, for a time.
items.ref: Real history (Battle of Mohi, 1241); Vencel Rikard from Transylvania by Night (Dark Ages) p. 105; the setback is a house reading.
items.fits: Fits the Mongol invasion card of 1241.

items.title: Jerusalem sacked
items.text: Khwarazmian horsemen sack Jerusalem in August 1244, and the crusader army is broken at La Forbie in October. The city will not be Christian again in this age.
items.fits: Fits the Order of Saint Lazarus card: its men die at Gaza (La Forbie) in 1244.

items.title: The Iglau mining code
items.text: The silver town of Jihlava (Iglau) sets down its mining law, which becomes the rule for workings across Moravia and Bohemia. Rothenstein's German council claims the Adit under it.
items.ref: Real history (Jihlava mining law, about 1249); the Adit claim is a house rule.
items.fits: Explains why the council holds the Adit on paper.

items.title: Tariq at Mansourah
items.text: In February 1250 the army of Louis IX is trapped at Mansourah and broken. Tariq fights in the city's defence; later Tariq serves the Old Man of the Mountain.
items.ref: Kindred Most Wanted p. 68; the battle of Mansourah, 1250, is real history.
items.fits: The book ties it to the Seventh Crusade.

items.title: The Mamluks
items.text: The Mamluk soldiers of Egypt take power in 1250. Ten years later, on 3 September 1260, they stop the Mongols at Ain Jalut. The mummies of Egypt count it a reprieve.
items.ref: Real history (1250, 1260); the mummies are a house reading.

items.title: The mortal Alamut falls
items.text: Hulegu's Mongols take the Nizari castle of Alamut in December 1256. Kindred in the east note that the Assamites did not stir: whatever their Alamut is, it is not this one.
items.ref: Real history (fall of Alamut, 1256); the Kindred reading is a house rule.
items.fits: Leaves the Assamite Alamut of the books untouched.

items.title: The House of Wisdom drowned
items.text: The Mongols sack Baghdad in February 1258; the libraries go into the Tigris. Batini carry out what they can before the walls fall.
items.ref: Real history (sack of Baghdad, 1258); the Batini are a house reading.

items.title: The king falls on the Marchfeld
items.text: On 26 August 1278 King Premysl Otakar II dies fighting Rudolf of Habsburg. Bad years follow: regents plunder the land and famine reaches the margraviate.
items.fits: No book event in Bohemia that year.

items.title: Black Earth Boy and the end of the Song
items.text: The last Song fleet is lost at Yamen in 1279. In those years Black Earth Boy rises to the Hundred Clouds, as the Fourth Age turns.
items.ref: Dharma Book: Thrashing Dragons p. 18 (the rise); the year is a house reading; the battle of Yamen, 1279, is real history.
items.fits: Before the Treaty of the Quincunx, 1304.

items.title: The divine wind
items.text: Two Mongol fleets sent against Japan, in 1274 and 1281, are wrecked by storms. Japan's priests and its spirits both claim the victory.
items.ref: Real history (1274, 1281); the claim is a house reading.

items.title: Kutna Hora silver and the Prague groschen
items.text: The great strike at Kutna Hora and the new Prague groschen of 1300 pull miners away from smaller workings. The Adit's silver is worth less and its miners drift away.
items.ref: Real history (Prague groschen, 1300); the Adit's decline is a house rule.
items.fits: Money by era already uses the groschen.

items.title: Murder at Olomouc
items.text: On 4 August 1306 the young King Wenceslas III is stabbed in Olomouc and the Premyslid line ends. Kindred of the march whisper that a Cainite hand guided the knife; no one proves it.
items.ref: Real history (death of Wenceslas III, 1306); the whisper is a house rule.
items.fits: Left as a rumour, so it binds no clan.

items.title: The Luxembourg kings
items.text: John of Luxembourg takes the Bohemian crown. German settlers keep arriving, and the towns and the old Moravian villages grow further apart.
items.ref: Real history (John of Luxembourg crowned, 1311; elected 1310).
items.fits: Feeds the council against the villages.

items.title: The last Grand Master burns
items.text: Jacques de Molay is burned in Paris on 18 March 1314. The tale that the Grand Master cursed king and pope from the fire, and that both died within the year, runs through Europe.
items.ref: Real history (1314); the curse is a legend.
items.fits: Follows the fall of the Temple, 1307.

items.title: A citadel in the Moravian Shadowlands
items.text: A legion of the Hierarchy raises a citadel in the Shadowlands of Moravia to hold the restless dead of the mines. It will outlast nearly every other in the east.
items.fits: Sets up the Future Darkness cards where Moravia is the Hierarchy's last fortress.

items.title: Mansa Musa in Cairo
items.text: Mansa Musa of Mali passes through Cairo on pilgrimage in 1324 with so much gold that its price falls for years.

items.title: Preachers against the Waldensians
items.text: Dominican inquisitors work the Bohemian crown lands against Waldensian heretics. One passes through the valley, asks the parish many questions, and writes down the answers.
items.ref: Real history in outline (inquisitors against Waldensians in Bohemia, 1330s); the visit is a house rule.
items.fits: Hunters before 1450 are the Inquisition's, per the standing rule.

items.title: The war of a hundred years begins
items.text: Philip VI takes Gascony from Edward III in May 1337. War between England and France goes on, with truces, until 1453.
items.fits: Runs under the France in the Age of Masks cards.

items.title: Prague becomes an archbishopric
items.text: On 30 April 1344 Prague is raised to an archbishopric over the bishops of Olomouc and Litomysl. The parish of St. Aegidius now answers to a church of its own crown.

items.title: The crossroads trod grows faint
items.text: The last trod near the valley, at the old crossroads, opens on fewer nights each year. The fae who use it feel the cold coming.

book.title: Constantinople in 1197
book.text: Around 1197 the city stands at the edge of ruin, threatening to drag the Dream down with it.

book.title: Time-Motion Managers (first edition)
book.text: The mechanical clock began with Benedictine monks around 1200 to time prayers; some say it also served Time magick.

book.title: The Latin Empire
book.text: The crusaders took Byzantium in 1204 and set up a feudal Latin Empire, also called Romania, with the emperor above vassals such as the King of Thessalonica and the Prince of Achaia.

book.title: The Latin Empire
book.text: The Toreador Methuselah Michael, the Patriarch of Constantinople, met Final Death in 1204, but that influence lingers.

book.title: Constantinople after the Dream
book.text: Ghouls abandoned when the Trinity families burned or fled in 1204 now hunt Cainites from the Grand Bazaar.

book.title: The Heretical end times
book.text: Most Heretics expect the Third Caine to appear in 1206 and dwell on earth for thirty-three years, like Christ.

book.title: Haunted places of the Isles
book.text: Bramber Castle in Sussex is said to hold the ghosts of three de Braose children starved by King John and of Lady Maud de Hurst, murdered in 1210.

book.title: Fall of Mistridge
book.text: The Hermetic sanctum at Mistridge fell in 1210, brought down by mortals led by a group calling itself the Craftmasons.

book.title: Gunpowder and siege
book.text: Mages have already used magic to build such weapons, and several cannon were fired in the destruction of the Mistridge Covenant in 1210.

book.title: Road to the Council
book.text: The Craftmasons destroyed Mistridge in the winter of 1210, and the Convention of the White Tower met on 25 March 1325.

book.title: Masters the Artisans honour
book.text: Roger Bacon's influence among the High Artisans remains immense; the Craftmasons showed their strength in 1210 when they brought down Mistridge with cannon.

book.title: The Holy Roman Empire in 1230
book.text: A moderate Ventrue faction, the Antasians, watched over the crowning of Frederick II at Frankfurt in 1212.

book.title: The Holy Roman Empire in 1230
book.text: After the Children's Crusade of 1212, Giselher, Ventrue prince of Cologne, barred Clan Lasombra from the city. Giselher never proved the Magisters were behind it, but used the charge against rivals anyway.

book.title: The Balm of Gilead
book.text: Before 1215 the vial was widely believed to have reached Cistercian monks near the start of the 12th century, though how it got there is unclear.

book.title: Marc de Brabant
book.text: Given as a child to a Benedictine priory in the twelfth century, Marc ran away at sixteen and was Embraced in 1216 by Megan of Bristol, a Gangrel of the 10th Generation.

book.title: Eye for the Weakness of Steel
book.text: It began among the Fellowship of Our Lady, a company of Toreador and Ventrue, and it passed to their successors after the Fellowship broke apart in 1218 through infighting.

book.title: France in 1230
book.text: Paris is the seat of the joint Toreador and Ventrue Grand Court. Geoffrey, a Ventrue, has led it as Prince of Paris since 1222, after overthrowing Alexander, Geoffrey's own sire.

book.title: Catherine Maidstone
book.text: A Toreador of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1229 by Maiselle of Rochester, born in the village of Strood.

book.title: Camilla and Cretheus
book.text: Cretheus, Fifth Generation Ventrue and childe of Mithras, ruled Rome in fact for nearly 300 years and is the only public member of the Ignoti; bending the knee to Camilla in 1229 was read as the hidden ones' blessing.

book.title: The Oath-Truce
book.text: It began in AD 1130 and so will end around 1230.

book.title: Mages of the Dark Medieval
book.text: In 1230 common superstition supports belief in magic, which helps mages cast with impunity; only in later ages does belief turn against them.

book.title: The great killers
book.text: A few great diseases cause most deaths in 1230; some can empty a village in weeks, others leave victims wasted husks.

book.title: The Eclipse of 1230
book.text: In May of 1230 an eclipse darkens the sky so deeply that workers go home thinking night has come.

book.title: The Ten Tribes
book.text: The Garou of 1230 count Ten Tribes.

book.title: The Anda
book.text: They see this era as a time to feed on the spreading chaos and fear and to prepare for the Golden Horde, which turns west in 1235 and pulls back in 1242.

book.title: The Heretical end times
book.text: Counting from a creation date of 3761 B.C.E. and five stages of a thousand years each, Heretics expect the material world to end in 1239.

book.title: Garou and the Tatar Yoke
book.text: With Kin of their own among the Mongol clans, the Shadow Lords quietly backed the Tatar Yoke over Russia from about 1240 to 1480.

book.title: Dark Medieval Italy
book.text: By the 1240s Italy is only a name on the map; loyalty comes from the cities, swollen by migrants from the countryside.

book.title: Kupala's Eve and the Tzimisce revolt
book.text: The Mongol invasion of 1241 broke Tzimisce holdings in the east and nearly destroyed the elder known as the Butcher of Rus. Elders tightened their grip on their thralls in response.

book.title: Scáth, the Wandering City
book.text: A diary of 1242 tells of a coterie sent by an unnamed powerful patron, chasing clues through Dublin, Edinburgh and Norwich toward London.

book.title: The Order of Saint Lazarus
book.text: Most of its men-at-arms die at Gaza in 1244, and its time in the Holy Land is ending during the 13th century.

book.title: Nasch the Circassian
book.text: A Ventrue of the 7th Generation, Embraced in 1263 by Palamon the Copt; a few childhood memories of the mountains are all that remain from before Egypt.

book.title: Medieval schisms
book.text: Roger Bacon's London Accord of 1268 ended the war among England's artisan guilds; de Varre founded the Solificati in 1315, and they broke away from the Order of Reason in 1335.

book.title: The Hospitallers and the Teutonic Knights
book.text: Large endowments in Western Europe fund the Hospitallers' work in the East, a structure that lets the order outlast the loss of the Holy Land in 1291.

book.title: The Striders in the Crusades
book.text: Around 1300 the wandering Caern of Long Voyages was thrown into an attack on a Zmei's servants in southern Russia and lost with its whole sept.

book.title: Raise the Sun
book.text: The last reliable account dates to about 1300, back when the tribe still kept its alliance with Helios and the Mound Builder Dreamspeakers.

book.title: The Treaty of the Quincunx
book.text: In 1304, ten years after Kublai Khan died, ancestors from three courts (Yellow Emperor, White Tiger and Black Tortoise) met at the Shaolin monastery near Changan and signed the Treaty of the Quincunx.

book.title: The fall of the Temple, 1307
book.text: King Philip the Fair had the French Templars seized in 1307 on heresy charges, with papal leave, and is widely thought to have wanted their wealth.

book.title: Templars as a Craft
book.text: In 1307 Philip the Fair had the French Templars arrested for heresy; some say vampire advisors or Batini with grudges pushed the king.

book.title: The Way of the Ancient Lawgivers
book.text: Founded in 1312, it holds that all Kindred must return to the ways of the First City, when mortals and lesser vampires honoured the Antediluvians.

book.title: The Chodona
book.text: Ten years on they wrote that purpose down as the Chodona, the Wheel of the Law with eight spokes; by 1314 the Wheel stretched from Nepal to Ireland.

book.title: Baerwald
book.text: Pagans gathered there as a refuge from persecution, and in 1317 Sir Garland declared the land a fief named Baerwald, an open insult to Rome and the Empire.

book.title: Chaoticians
book.text: In 1325, as that Order formally began, mathematicians made a sub-lodge, the Arithmeticians, never strong enough to be a Convention.

book.title: Vincent Day
book.text: A Ventrue antitribu of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1327 by Leander Phipps, once a Templar in the Crusades.

book.title: Medieval schisms
book.text: The Paris University Purge of 1330 killed many mages and destroyed the Hermetic covenant of Le Ictus.

book.title: War of the Dust Witch
book.text: The War of the Dust Witch near Great Zimbabwe, 1345 to 1350, split the Ngoma and the Madzimbabwe into separate groups; plague in 1420 set them at war, each blaming the other.

items.title: A university in Prague
items.text: On 7 April 1348 Charles IV founds the university in Prague. Hermetic masters and the first members of the Order of Reason both send students there to watch each other.
items.ref: Real history (Charles University, 1348); the mages are a house rule.
items.fits: The Order of Reason is formed by 1325 on the approved cards.

items.title: Plague in Cairo and Damascus
items.text: The Black Death reaches Cairo and Damascus in 1348; Cairo may lose a third of its people. The dead of the Nile go into the Underworld with those of Europe.
items.fits: Follows the Black Death and the Second Great Maelstrom of 1347.

items.title: The plague reaches Moravia
items.text: The Black Death reaches Moravia in 1349 and 1350, lighter than in the west but bad in the towns. The Herd thins, the parish buries in pits, and the Shadowlands fill.
items.fits: Follows the Black Death and the Second Great Maelstrom of 1347.

items.title: The trod closes
items.text: At the Shattering the crossroads trod closes. The valley's fae who stay hide in mortal bodies among the old families.

items.title: An emperor from Prague
items.text: Charles IV is crowned emperor in Rome in 1355. Prague is the Empire's capital, and Kindred of the west take more notice of the east.
items.ref: Real history (imperial coronation of Charles IV, 1355).

items.title: The Jacquerie
items.text: In May and June 1358 the peasants of northern France rise and are crushed by the nobles.

items.title: The Ming
items.text: Zhu Yuanzhang drives the Mongols from Beijing and founds the Ming in 1368. The courts of the Middle Kingdom hold that the Quincunx kept their quarrels from spoiling the change.
items.ref: Real history (1368); the courts' reading is a house rule.
items.fits: After the Treaty of the Quincunx, 1304.

items.title: Timur
items.text: Timur takes power at Samarkand in 1370. Delhi is sacked in December 1398, Baghdad and Damascus in 1401; towers of skulls mark the road.

items.title: The peasants rise in England
items.text: The Peasants' Revolt takes London in June 1381. Elders of the west see the same thing in their own childer that summer: the Anarch Revolt begins.
items.ref: Real history (Peasants' Revolt, 1381); the link is a house reading.
items.fits: The Anarch Revolt begins in 1381 on the approved cards.

items.title: Kosovo Field
items.text: The Serbs and the Ottomans meet at Kosovo on 15 June 1389; both rulers die. The Ottomans come on into the Balkans.

items.title: Ankara
items.text: Timur beats and captures the Ottoman sultan Bayezid at Ankara on 20 July 1402. The Ottomans need ten years to recover.

items.title: The revolt reaches the march
items.text: The Anarch Revolt, begun in 1381, reaches Moravia. Young Kindred and their ghouls rise against the Tzimisce of the hills; some lords are burned in their beds, some hold.

items.title: The treasure fleets
items.text: Zheng He's fleets sail from China to India, Arabia and East Africa, seven times between 1405 and 1433, and then sail no more.

items.title: Grunwald
items.text: Poland and Lithuania break the Teutonic Order at Grunwald (Tannenberg) on 15 July 1410.
items.fits: Fits the Hospitallers and the Teutonic Order card.

items.title: Jan Hus is burned
items.text: On 6 July 1415 Jan Hus is burned at Constance. Preachers of his cause reach the valley within the year.

items.title: The Hussite wars
items.text: On 30 July 1419 the councillors of Prague New Town are thrown from the windows, and war follows until Lipany in May 1434. Moravia splits between Catholic lords and Hussite towns; the parish and the council take opposite sides.
items.ref: Real history (first defenestration of Prague, 1419; Battle of Lipany, 1434).

items.title: War wagons and handguns
items.text: The Craftmasons watch the Hussite war wagons and handguns closely, and some of the Hussite smiths hear from them. The Order of Hermes watches the Craftmasons.
items.fits: Fits the Order of Reason's rise on the approved cards.

items.title: Heretics everywhere
items.text: In the war years the Church sees heresy in every town. Its hunters in Moravia find more Hussites than monsters, but now and then a monster.

items.title: The Maid is burned
items.text: Joan of Arc relieves Orleans in May 1429 and is burned at Rouen on 30 May 1431. The Church's hunters argue for years over what spoke to her.
items.ref: Real history (1429, 1431); the hunters are a house reading.

items.title: The march stays outside
items.text: When the Camarilla forms, the Tzimisce of the Moravian hills refuse it. The march is left to them, and to the families who hide them.
items.fits: After the Camarilla is formed in 1435.

items.title: The citadel holds
items.text: Through the plague years and the war the Hierarchy's Moravian citadel takes in the dead of the battlefields and grows strong.
items.fits: Keeps the citadel of d10 in play.

items.title: A Korean alphabet
items.text: King Sejong publishes Hangul in 1446, an alphabet made so that common people can read.

book.title: The Black Death and the Second Great Maelstrom
book.text: Plague reaches Europe. The dead cross the Shroud in such numbers that the Second Great Maelstrom breaks over the Underworld.

book.title: The Shattering
book.text: Banality closes the ways to Arcadia. The last open trods fail and the fae who stay must hide in mortal bodies.

book.title: Roderigo al-Dakhil
book.text: Once a Castilian soldier fighting to retake Cadiz, Roderigo was Embraced in 1354 by Mokhadaji Ranpur, a Nagaraja of the 6th Generation.

book.title: War of the Dust Witch
book.text: The Screaming Ghost Purge of 1356 to 1360 set Dalou'laoshi and Wu Lung against the Akashics and drove the Brotherhood back into Tibet.

book.title: The Convention of Thorns
book.text: Brujah signed twice, since clan members sat on both sides of the table. Most European Kindred active when the revolt began in 1381 were dead by its end in 1493.

book.title: Knights of St. George
book.text: The Resolute Knights of St. George were founded in Syria in the 11th century and by the 1400s had houses from Ireland to India.

book.title: Mukhtar Bey
book.text: Mukhtar Bey has held the domain since first claiming it in 1406.

book.title: The Camarilla is formed
book.text: Elders of several clans bind themselves into one sect to hide the Kindred from the Inquisition.

book.title: Lady Nightshade
book.text: Lady Nightshade's story begins in Harrogate, England, at Midsummer of 1435.

book.title: Road to the Council
book.text: In 1440 the Hermetic master Baldric met Lady Nightshade of the Verbena and Master Valorian of the Chorus in the ruins of Mistridge, where fae are said to have visited them, and the three agreed to found an order.

book.title: The fall of the Cappadocians
book.text: Augustus Giovanni diablerizes Cappadocius. The Giovanni set out to destroy what is left of the clan.

book.title: Augustus and the Promise of 1528
book.text: Augustus Giovanni diablerized the Cappadocian founder in 1444, rising to the Third Generation and splitting the old clan from the Venetian family.

book.title: The Premascines
book.text: Giovanni tell of kin who helped Augustus rise against the founder, Embraced before 1444, and so perhaps of the Fourth or Fifth Generation. Accounts give anywhere from four to twelve of them.

book.title: The founding wars
book.text: Daedalean forces took Doissetep in 1448; the physical fortress fell and the main keep moved to a Horizon Realm.

book.title: The founding wars
book.text: The Second Mistridge Convocation in 1449 came under attack by Craftmasons and Artificers; the mystics won at heavy cost and helped build Horizon afterward.

items.title: Constantinople falls
items.text: The Ottomans take Constantinople on 29 May 1453. The last Cainites who still remember the Dream leave by sea, or stay and bargain with the new masters.
items.ref: Real history (1453); the Cainites are a house reading.
items.fits: Long after the Dream ends in 1204 on the approved cards.

items.title: The printed Bible
items.text: Gutenberg's Bible comes off the press in Mainz about 1455. The Order of Reason sees at once what books by the thousand will do to belief.
items.ref: Real history (about 1455); the mages are a house reading.

items.title: A Hussite king
items.text: George of Podebrady is elected King of Bohemia on 2 March 1458. Rome calls him a heretic, and the Catholic lords of Moravia turn to Hungary.
items.ref: Real history (election of George of Podebrady, 1458).

items.title: The Hungarian years
items.text: Matthias Corvinus is chosen king in Olomouc in 1469 and holds Moravia until the Peace of Olomouc in 1479. Hungarian soldiers are quartered in the towns.
items.ref: Real history (Matthias Corvinus in Moravia, 1469 to 1479).

items.title: The Spanish Inquisition
items.text: The Spanish Inquisition is set up in 1478; Granada falls on 2 January 1492 and the Jews are expelled that year. Rafael de Corazon, a Toreador of the old Spanish wars, urges the elders to give up open ties to mortals and pass into shadow.
items.ref: Real history (1478, 1492); Rafael de Corazon from Children of the Inquisition p. 35; the timing is a house reading.
items.fits: Before the first Camarilla Conclave of 1486.

items.title: Old Clan in the hills
items.text: After the Convention of Thorns most Tzimisce join the Sabbat. Some in Moravia refuse both sects and keep the old ways, hidden by the families who have always fed and sheltered them.
items.fits: Fits the 1493 Convention of Thorns and the Old Clan Tzimisce of 1989 on the approved cards; sets up the Future Darkness card on the old families who hid Kindred for centuries.

items.title: Vasantasena goes over
items.text: At the founding of the Sabbat the Malkavian seer Vasantasena, who had helped rally the clan behind the Camarilla, leaves it over its disbelief in the Antediluvians and leads a brood of anarchs into the new sect.
items.ref: Clanbook: Malkavian (Revised) p. 98; the year is a house reading.

items.title: Da Gama at Calicut
items.text: Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut in May 1498. Portuguese guns come to the Indian Ocean.

items.title: The Safavids
items.text: Ismail is crowned shah at Tabriz in 1501 and makes Twelver Shia faith the law of Persia.

items.title: The Ottomans take Cairo
items.text: Selim I takes Cairo in January 1517 and ends the Mamluk state. Mukhtar Bey, who has held the city since 1406, spreads influence beyond Egypt under the new rulers.
items.ref: Real history (1517); Cairo by Night pp. 44, 74.

items.title: Luther
items.text: On 31 October 1517 Martin Luther posts the theses at Wittenberg. Western Christendom splits.

items.title: The Habsburgs
items.text: After Mohacs, Ferdinand of Habsburg is chosen King of Bohemia in 1526. Vienna is now the crown's seat, and the march looks south.

items.title: Panipat
items.text: Babur defeats the Sultan of Delhi at Panipat on 21 April 1526 and founds the Mughal empire.

items.title: The Anabaptist households
items.text: Anabaptist communities settle in southern Moravia under the protection of local lords, living in shared households. They stay until they are driven out in 1622.
items.ref: Real history (Hutterite communities in Moravia, from 1528).

items.title: The Turks before Vienna
items.text: Suleiman besieges Vienna in September and October 1529 and fails. The Danube becomes a frontier.

items.title: Anne Boleyn
items.text: Anne Boleyn is beheaded in the Tower on 19 May 1536. The living say the queen haunts it; the Restless say the queen serves the Quiet Lord as an Anacreon of southern England.
items.ref: Real history (1536); Love Beyond Death p. 68 (the Restless' account).

items.title: Guns in Japan
items.text: Portuguese traders land on Tanegashima in 1543 and sell arquebuses. Within thirty years Japanese armies fight with them.

items.title: The caern and the deep shafts
items.text: New shafts below the Adit cut into ground the hill sept guards. The Garou drive the miners out twice; the third time they lose the caern's outer stone.

items.title: Lepanto
items.text: The Holy League destroys the Ottoman fleet at Lepanto on 7 October 1571.

items.title: Rudolf's Prague
items.text: Emperor Rudolf II moves the court to Prague in 1583. Alchemists, astrologers and astronomers gather there, and both the Traditions and the Order of Reason send people to court.
items.ref: Real history (Rudolf II's court in Prague, 1583 to 1612); the mages are a house rule.

items.title: The Golem tale
items.text: The tale of the rabbi of Prague who made a man of clay is told across the crown lands. Mages argue whether it is a story or a working.
items.ref: Legend (the Golem of Prague, set in Rabbi Loew's time); the reading is a house rule.
items.fits: Left open: no book card dates it.

items.title: The invasion of Korea
items.text: Japan invades Korea in 1592 and again in 1597. Admiral Yi's ships hold the sea.

items.title: Isfahan
items.text: Shah Abbas makes Isfahan the capital in 1598. Batini schools gather in the new city.
items.ref: Real history (1598); the Batini are a house reading.
items.fits: The Batini train Qutbs in Isfahan in 1979 on the approved cards.

items.title: The citadel through the storm
items.text: The Third Great Maelstrom batters Stygia. The Moravian citadel is cut off but stands, and its legion rules the eastern Shadowlands alone for a time.

items.title: Sekigahara
items.text: Tokugawa Ieyasu wins at Sekigahara on 21 October 1600; peace under the shoguns lasts two and a half centuries.

book.title: The making of Horizon
book.text: After the defeat of the Craftmasons in the Battle of Flames in 1450, the Primi of the Traditions resolved to build a Realm far from Earth as their meeting place.

book.title: The founding wars
book.text: Tezghul the Insane and Lithuanian demon-worshippers ravaged the Baltic from Kupala Alka from 1450 to 1453, and in 1452 the Daedaleans swore an Oath of Fire against vampires and magi.

book.title: The making of Horizon
book.text: At a minor Tribunal in the Gediz Caves in 1452 the Nodes, still called the Columns of Power, were formally dedicated; among them were Stonehenge and Glastonbury Tor.

book.title: The Servitors of Irad
book.text: Founded in 1456, the cult recruits no one openly and works to keep other Kindred weak and misled before Gehenna.

book.title: France in the Age of Masks
book.text: Louis XI takes the throne in 1461 and drags France into plots and near revolt; Charles VIII invades Italy to claim Naples, starting some 50 years of war that wins nothing lasting.

book.title: The Grand Convocation ends
book.text: After nine years of talks the mystic mages found the Council of Nine Traditions against the Order of Reason.

book.title: Parovich
book.text: A Nosferatu antitribu of the Seventh Generation, Embraced in 1467 by Boronisk, once an officer in the army of Ivan the Great.

book.title: The first Camarilla Conclave
book.text: The sect holds its first Conclave and names its first Justicars.

book.title: The Convention of Thorns
book.text: The Anarch Revolt ends at Thorns. The anarchs who refuse the treaty go on to found the Sabbat; the Assamites are cursed.

book.title: The Eldest and the du'at
book.text: Jamal, a warrior, held the Black Throne from 1494 to 1998. Ur-Shulgi says Jamal refused to renounce Allah and was destroyed for it; many schismatics call Jamal a martyr. Ur-Shulgi does not take the title, giving it to Haqim alone.

book.title: Hong Kong by Night
book.text: For about 1500 years Hong Kong was a backwater ruled from Canton, its villages farming and fishing while Canton grew into a great trading city.

book.title: Voragg the Unbound
book.text: Voragg has served the Wyrm for centuries, mostly while bound in a rock deep under the Rocky Mountains, where a Wendigo tribe sealed it after it troubled them in the late 1500s.

book.title: The Aztec Empire before Cortes
book.text: By 1519 more than forty conquered provinces paid tribute to the emperor, who would soon need a Flower War, a battle fought only to take captives for sacrifice, if no new states could be found to conquer.

book.title: Augustus and the Promise of 1528
book.text: Within decades other clans called the Necromancers Devil Kindred. To avoid a united front against them, the Giovanni swore in 1528 to stay forever outside Kindred affairs.

book.title: The Patmostine Order
book.text: It was founded in the 1530s, in the wake of the Reformation, by the French Toreador Louvel Tarneau.

book.title: Black Hand Ranks and Marks
book.text: The crescent tattoo of the Hand has been in use since at least about 1550.

book.title: The Twilight Cult
book.text: Founded in 1550, it believes a single Book of Nod stanza about the last daughter of Eve is the key: control or destroy that daughter and Gehenna is averted.

book.title: Seats won and lost
book.text: During the witch-hunts of the 1560s refugees flooded Horizon, and Doissetep, once called its sister Chantry, broke with it over a failed plan for European universities.

book.title: France in the Age of Masks
book.text: Catherine di Medici rules as regent for the young kings from 1560 to 1589, and the strife between Catholic nobles and Huguenots peaks in the St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre of 1572.

book.title: Cockatrice
book.text: The last mortal record of one is a Warsaw church entry from 1587. Survivors now lurk in rural Chantries and unsettled Realms, where they plague mages in their sanctuaries.

book.title: The Croatan give themselves at Roanoke
book.text: The whole tribe dies to stop a great servant of the Wyrm. No living Croatan remains.

book.title: The Third Great Maelstrom
book.text: After the Looting, the Breaking of the Guilds and the Flaying of Obsidian, the worst storm yet cuts Stygia off. The Shroud thickens.

book.title: Polonia
book.text: Polonia is of the 7th generation, Embraced in 1600 by Anton de Concepcion.

book.title: Justicars
book.text: Archons, the justicars' agents, are usually picked from promising ancillae and young elders. They existed long before the title, which came into use in the late 1600s, probably from the Brujah.

book.title: The Sabbat of Ville-Marie
book.text: By the middle of the 1600s, tales of torture and of children shaped into living mounds of bone and flesh reached Camarilla ears in France. The Toreador investigated, found signs of unsanctioned emigration, and put pawns in key posts to take hold of the colony.

book.title: Raymond Narcisse
book.text: Once Father Raymond, a convert born in the West Indies, recruited from a Norman monastery for Pierre de l'Ancre's witch hunts in Labourd in the early 1600s.

items.title: The moons of Jupiter
items.text: Galileo publishes the moons of Jupiter in March 1610. The Order of Reason calls it proof; the Celestial Chorus calls it a trespass.
items.ref: Real history (1610); the mages are a house reading.

items.title: Defenestration and war
items.text: On 23 May 1618 the Bohemian estates throw the emperor's regents from a window of Prague Castle. The Thirty Years War begins.

items.title: White Mountain and after
items.text: The Bohemian estates lose at White Mountain on 8 November 1620. Protestant lords are executed in 1621, the Anabaptists are expelled in 1622, and the Renewed Land Ordinance follows (Moravia, 1628).

items.title: Japan closes
items.text: After the Shimabara rising of 1637 and 1638, Japan closes its ports to nearly all foreigners in 1639.

items.title: The Swedes in Olomouc
items.text: Swedish troops take Olomouc in June 1642 and hold it until 1650. Foragers reach the valley; the families hide their stores, their daughters and sons, and their Kindred.
items.ref: Real history (Swedish occupation of Olomouc, 1642 to 1650).

items.title: Beijing falls
items.text: Rebels take Beijing in 1644 and the last Ming emperor dies; the Manchu Qing take the city weeks later. The courts of the Middle Kingdom read the omens and wait.
items.ref: Real history (1644); the courts are a house reading.

items.title: Brno holds
items.text: The Swedes besiege Brno in 1645 and fail. The town is remembered for it for centuries.

items.title: Westphalia
items.text: The Peace of Westphalia in October 1648 ends the Thirty Years War.

items.title: The Great Fire
items.text: London burns from 2 to 6 September 1666. Prince Mithras's Kindred lose havens in the City, and some say a few of them lit the fire.
items.ref: Real history (1666); the Kindred are a house reading.

items.title: The Losiny trials
items.text: From 1678 to 1696 witch trials in northern Moravia send about a hundred people to the fire. Kindred and fae keep very still while the inquisitor works.
items.ref: Real history (witch trials of Velke Losiny and Sumperk, 1678 to 1696).
items.fits: No clash; mortal hunters, not the imbued.

items.title: The plague of 1680
items.text: Plague spreads from Vienna through the crown lands in 1679 and 1680. Plague columns go up in the squares afterwards.

items.title: Kahlenberg
items.text: The Ottoman army is beaten before Vienna on 12 September 1683. The Turks are pushed back down the Danube.

items.title: Alexis Danpai abroad
items.text: Peter the Great sends young Russians west to learn shipbuilding and statecraft. Alexis Danpai, of a family the tsar favours, is among them.
items.ref: Kindred Most Wanted p. 56; the year is a house reading.
items.fits: The book has Alexis born at the start of the 18th century.

items.title: Nader Shah in Delhi
items.text: Nader Shah of Persia sacks Delhi in 1739 and carries off the Peacock Throne.

items.title: The Prussians come
items.text: Frederick of Prussia invades Moravia in 1742 and besieges Brno, and comes back against Olomouc in 1758. Each time the countryside pays.

items.title: Lisbon
items.text: An earthquake, fire and sea wave destroy Lisbon on 1 November 1755, All Saints' Day. Europe's thinkers argue over what God allows.

items.title: Plassey
items.text: The East India Company wins at Plassey on 23 June 1757. The Order of Reason's merchants follow the Company into Bengal.
items.ref: Real history (1757); the mages are a house reading.
items.fits: Fits the Mage history from 1756 card.

items.title: Joseph's patents
items.text: Joseph II ends personal serfdom and grants toleration to Protestants in 1781, and soon after closes many monasteries. Peasants may now leave the land; some leave the valley.
items.ref: Real history (patents of toleration and on serfdom, 1781).

items.title: The Bastille
items.text: Paris takes the Bastille on 14 July 1789. The Terror follows in 1793 and 1794.

items.title: Wool mills in Brno
items.text: Brno's cloth mills grow, and the Order of Reason takes an interest in Moravian manufacture. The valley's weavers feel it first in their prices.
items.ref: Real history in outline (Brno's cloth industry); the mages are a house rule.

items.title: Germaine is Embraced
items.text: In the Revolution the Brujah Critias Embraces Germaine; the Countess d'Adhemar, a Toreador childe of Madame Guil, is the lover Critias keeps.
items.ref: Dread Names, Red List p. 49; the year is a house reading inside the Revolution.

items.title: Napoleon in Egypt
items.text: Napoleon lands in Egypt in July 1798 and wins at the Pyramids; his scholars find the Rosetta Stone in 1799. The mummies watch strangers dig.
items.ref: Real history (1798, 1799); the mummies are a house reading.

items.title: Austerlitz
items.text: On 2 December 1805 Napoleon beats the Austrian and Russian armies at Austerlitz (Slavkov), east of Brno. Thousands of the dead go into the Moravian Shadowlands in one day.

items.title: The legion of Austerlitz
items.text: The Moravian citadel takes in the soldiers of Austerlitz and forms a new legion from them. The Hierarchy in the east is stronger for it.
items.fits: Keeps the citadel of d10 in play.

items.title: Moscow burns
items.text: Napoleon enters Moscow in September 1812 and finds it burning. The retreat that winter kills most of his army.

items.title: Waterloo and the year without a summer
items.text: Napoleon is beaten at Waterloo on 18 June 1815. The eruption of Tambora that April darkens the next year; 1816 has no summer across Europe.

items.title: The hieroglyphs read
items.text: Champollion reads the hieroglyphs in 1822. For the first time since antiquity, the living can read the mummies' names.
items.ref: Real history (1822); the mummies are a house reading.

book.title: Maryann Fletcher
book.text: A Nosferatu of the 8th Generation, Embraced in 1614 by Stanford Warwick, who found Maryann burned yet alive in a tavern after a Ventrue purge of the sire's servants.

book.title: Jeremy MacNeil
book.text: Jeremy MacNeil is a Brujah of the Eighth Generation, born in 1631 and Embraced in 1657.

book.title: The blood gods of Tenochtitlan
book.text: During an eclipse on 23 August 1691, tendrils of shadow impaled Lasombra in their crypts, and three died. Goratrix and the Tremere antitribu later claimed to have destroyed Tezcatlipoca with a ritual using the black ichor from the wounds; they showed no proof, but Tezcatlipoca was never seen again.

book.title: The Aztec Fiends
book.text: Through the 1700s the Lasombra and Tzimisce fought a war of pawns inside the colonial Church, Lasombra backing Spanish-born priests and the Tzimisce stirring up creole ones, until armed priests clashed and the army stepped in.

book.title: The Hippocratic Circle's long past
book.text: Racism and sexism took hold in the Circle in the 1700s, demeaning its women and its non-European forebears, now called the Aesculapians.

book.title: Doran
book.text: Doran crossed to North America and in the early 1700s went south rather than north to Canada, settling in the Louisiana territory.

book.title: The Taking of California
book.text: Ever since Spanish monks came early in the 1700s, Old World undead have ruled the New World's mortals by murder and deceit, hidden behind the Masquerade.

book.title: Simon de Cosa
book.text: Cosa attacked Doran in 1713, and for years their mortal followers clashed. Cosa had Bienville removed from office and a servant of Cosa's own, Antoine Cadillac, made governor.

book.title: The Hippocratic Circle's long past
book.text: Life-extension work let leading Technocrats live for centuries; Reginald Proctor, extended in 1715, was the only one lost before the Anomaly, by suicide in 1914.

book.title: Edgardo Robbia
book.text: A Brujah of the 8th Generation, Embraced in 1736 by Katherine Wiese, who released Edgardo early in the nineteenth century.

book.title: Doran
book.text: Early in a long war with the Brujah Simon de Cosa, Doran made the governor, Bienville, a ghoul. In 1743 Bienville broke free with a mage's help and returned to Europe.

book.title: The bayou treaty
book.text: Werewolves followed their Cajun kinfolk to the bayous after 1755 and fought the Uktena already there over a caern. In the end the vampires and the Uktena together pushed Cosa into the western swamps.

book.title: Mage history from 1756
book.text: In 1756 more than a hundred Native American Dreamspeakers left Horizon over bias against tribal and shamanic magic.

book.title: Cock Robin
book.text: Robin was a silversmith's apprentice in colonial America, Embraced in 1757 during the French and English war for the continent and then abandoned by the sire.

book.title: Simon de Cosa
book.text: Idealist elders in Spain who hoped to settle in Louisiana had France cede the territory to Spain in 1763. Doran's servants lost their offices, and Cosa rose again and drove the Ventrue from the city.

book.title: Tatiana Stepanova
book.text: A Ravnos of the Eighth Generation, Embraced in 1764 by Vasily Vasilevich, born to a noble family.

book.title: The Josians
book.text: The Inner Circle founded the order at its 1764 gathering, when the Hellfire Clubs were in fashion; rumour credits Meerlinda with the name.

book.title: Germaine
book.text: When Louis XVI took the throne in 1774, the Toreador of the French court backed the status quo against reform.

book.title: The Gumagan
book.text: Gumagan live in the deserts, Arnhem Land, New Guinea and the Torres Strait Islands; none have been left in southern Australia since the war that began in 1788.

book.title: Laurette Morel
book.text: A Toreador of the 8th Generation, Embraced in 1790 by Émeric de Sauveterre, at home on the Côte d'Azur among the very rich; Villon sees a former Anarch self in Laurette.

book.title: Stargazers of Australia
book.text: Luther Gazes-Inward, the first Stargazer in Australia, landed at Sydney Town in 1790, and the tribe hoped to learn from the Aboriginal peoples and the Bunyip, who would not speak with them.

book.title: House Genji
book.text: They took the name of the first Genji, vampires who had driven out the Bishamon centuries before, and their power grew with Japan's rise in the late 1800s and early 1900s.

book.title: The New World Order's rise
book.text: Its power grew through the 1800s as it infiltrated groups, among them the first mixed Tradition Chantries, and it became the Technocracy's internal police.

book.title: Chaoticians
book.text: In the 1800s they joined others around the computer to become the Difference Engineers, finally finding a place in the Union.

book.title: Ayisha Jocastian
book.text: A Turkish Cypriot born under Ottoman rule in the 1800s and among the best-known vampires of the modern era.

book.title: Bone Gnawer Kin in Other Lines
book.text: By the late 1800s the tribe had Kin among Irish and Scottish families, and descendants who earned glory were often taken in by the Fianna, so many Garou carry a Bone Gnawer ancestor they would rather hide.

book.title: Brujah of the West
book.text: The western Brujah are younger than most clans of the Camarilla; those Embraced in the 1800s barely know the old tragedies of their line.

book.title: Andrew Seneca
book.text: Born a slave on a Georgia cotton plantation and taken into the house as manservant to Jackson Mills; Embraced in 1807 by Monica San Valentin, Ventrue of the 8th Generation.

book.title: Esperanza Lucifer
book.text: Lasombra of the 5th Generation, Embraced in 1812 by one known as Mary; when one Esperanza Lucifer falls, a new one takes up the fearsome role.

book.title: Mage history from 1756
book.text: The Seers of Chronos became the Sahajiya in 1825, then the Cultists of Bacchus, then the Cult of Ecstasy.

book.title: Don Sebastian
book.text: Don Sebastian was a Californio landowner who sheltered the survivors of the brig Danube, wrecked in San Pedro Bay on Christmas Day 1828.

book.title: The Storm Eater’s escape
book.text: It broke free some time in the 1830s, as caern after caern fell to the European Garou, and the Garou needed decades even to learn its name.

book.title: The Storm Eater reborn
book.text: In the 1830s the Europeans’ seizure of too many Uktena and Wendigo caerns weakened the seals, and the Bane slipped out and began feeding again.

book.title: Mage history from 1756
book.text: Babbage and Lovelace's work in 1834 gave rise to the Difference Engineers, who became the Virtual Adepts around 1880; the Natural Philosophers renamed themselves Electrodyne Engineers in 1866.

book.title: Seneschal
book.text: Princes cite the Nuremberg affair of 1836, when a Sabbat spy became seneschal and passed what was learned to the sect.

items.title: The railway reaches Brno
items.text: The Emperor Ferdinand Northern Railway opens from Vienna to Brno in July 1839. News, goods and travellers now come in days, not weeks.
items.fits: Travel by era already uses railways from this span.

items.title: The Opium War
items.text: Britain goes to war with China over opium in 1839. Hong Kong is ceded in 1842.
items.fits: Fits the Hong Kong by Night card.

items.title: The Great Hunger
items.text: Blight takes the Irish potato from 1845; a million die and a million leave. The Fianna lose Kinfolk to the ships.
items.ref: Real history (1845 to 1849); the Fianna are a house reading.
items.fits: Fits the Bone Gnawer Kin card on Irish families.

items.title: The year of revolutions
items.text: In 1848 the labour dues are abolished (September) and an imperial parliament meets at Kromeriz in Moravia until it is closed in March 1849.
items.ref: Real history (end of labour dues, 1848; Kromeriz parliament, 1848 to 1849).

items.title: The springtime of peoples
items.text: Revolution breaks out in Paris in February 1848 and spreads to Vienna, Berlin, Milan and Budapest. Most of it is put down within a year.

items.title: The Taiping
items.text: The Taiping rebellion grows from 1850 into a civil war that kills tens of millions before 1864.

items.title: The Indian rising
items.text: The sepoys rise at Meerut in May 1857; the war lasts a year, and the Crown takes India from the Company in 1858.

items.title: Peas in a monastery garden
items.text: Gregor Mendel reads his work on heredity in pea plants to the Brno society in 1865. Almost no one notices; a few Progenitors do.
items.ref: Real history (Mendel's lectures, 1865); the Progenitors are a house rule.

items.title: Prussians and cholera
items.text: Prussia beats Austria in the war of 1866 and occupies Brno; cholera follows the armies.

items.title: Hakari in the new capital
items.text: In the Meiji Restoration of 1868 the emperor moves to Edo, now Tokyo. Hakari, oldest of the undead in Japan, keeps court in the Imperial Palace from then on.
items.ref: Real history (1868); Hakari from Encyclopaedia Vampirica p. 89; the timing is a house reading.
items.fits: Fits House Genji's rise with Japan in the late 1800s.

items.title: The Suez Canal
items.text: The Suez Canal opens on 17 November 1869. Europe and Asia are weeks closer.

items.title: The Commune
items.text: Paris rises as the Commune in March 1871; the army takes the city back in the Bloody Week of May.

items.title: The tsar is killed
items.text: Alexander II is killed by a bomb in St. Petersburg on 13 March 1881. Pogroms follow in the south.

items.title: Krakatoa
items.text: Krakatoa explodes on 27 August 1883; red sunsets circle the world for months.

items.title: Ostrava's furnaces
items.text: Coal and iron at Ostrava grow into a black country. The hill sept smells the Wyrm in the pits and the Weaver in the furnaces.
items.ref: Real history in outline (Ostrava industry); the Garou are a house rule.

items.title: The Adit closes
items.text: The valley's mine is worked out and closed. The miners' families leave for Ostrava and Brno, and the Adit becomes a place children are told to keep away from.

items.title: Theo Bell in London
items.text: Don Cerro brings the childe Theo Bell to Victorian London to learn to read Kindred society. In London Bell meets Angus Abranson, a friendship that lasts a century.
items.ref: Clan Novel Trilogy: Brujah 1, Slave Ring p. 35, and Brujah 2, The Overseer; the year is a house reading.
items.fits: The book has them meet about a hundred years before the late 1990s.

items.title: Seances in Brno
items.text: Spiritualist circles meet in Brno and Olomouc. Some reach the restless dead of the Moravian citadel, which does not like it.
items.fits: Fits the Spiritualism in the West card, 1900.

items.title: The Boxers
items.text: The Boxer rising besieges the legations in Beijing in the summer of 1900.

items.title: Tsushima and Bloody Sunday
items.text: Japan sinks the Russian fleet at Tsushima in May 1905; in January troops fire on marchers in St. Petersburg and revolution follows.

items.title: Tunguska
items.text: Something bursts over the Siberian forest at Tunguska on 30 June 1908 and flattens it for miles. Every faction of mages has a theory.
items.ref: Real history (1908); the theories are a house reading.

items.title: The end of the Qing
items.text: Revolution breaks out at Wuchang in October 1911; the last emperor gives up the throne in February 1912.

book.title: Archbishop Strathcona
book.text: In the years before the Rebellions of 1837 and 1838, Strathcona watched the city's cliquish ancillae, likened to an old boys' club, spend their nights on their wealth at the Beaver Club and the Exchange Coffee House, and judged it time for the Sabbat to act.

book.title: The Gothic Victorian Age
book.text: Victoria has ruled the Empire's living subjects since 1837, so few alive remember any other reign.

book.title: Montreal (Sabbat city)
book.text: In an 1838 letter to Prince Mithras of London, Archbishop Strathcona claimed that Montreal had always belonged to the Sabbat and warned the Camarilla off, calling it the City of Black Miracles.

book.title: Archbishop Strathcona
book.text: Strathcona wrote to Prince Mithras of London in April 1838, declaring that once-friends were now dead to each other and that Montreal would be defended against the Camarilla.

book.title: San Francisco in the Gold Rush
book.text: In 1849 San Francisco grew from 900 people to 26,000, with another 100,000 passing through on the way to the hills.

book.title: Darklings in the occult revival
book.text: As the Order of Reason began turning into the Technocratic Union in the mid-1800s, several were caught in the fighting, and the survivors passed on a warning to stay out of wizards' affairs.

book.title: Financiers and the Proctor takeover
book.text: In 1851 the tangle of guild laws was folded into one body named the Financiers.

book.title: Alex Swift
book.text: A Virginian Confederate officer from 1861, friend to Stonewall Jackson, shot and left for dead at the Battle of Fisher's Hill.

book.title: Lady Margaret Willoughby
book.text: A Tremere of the 9th Generation, perhaps antitribu, Embraced in 1864; sire Lady Lise Paulmann is destroyed.

book.title: Badr al-Budur
book.text: An Assamite of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1867 by Ma'aruf, and of the same lineage as the notorious Fatima.

book.title: Miria, the Bygone Visions Caern
book.text: Shadow Lords have been barred from the island since their treachery in 1868, and Get of Fenris of both sexes since 1967, when Get women seeking sanctuary opened a moon bridge for their kin to seize it.

book.title: Don Sebastian
book.text: From 25 December 1870 Don Sebastian governed Los Angeles as prince, a stern but fair ruler to the refugees who came south from San Francisco, caring nothing for their pasts so long as they kept the rules of the domain.

book.title: The Giovanni of New York
book.text: Through paid dispatchers, customs men and dock and ground crews, the Giovanni have watched what moves up the Hudson since the 1870s and through Idlewild, now Kennedy, airport since 1962.

book.title: New York
book.text: Tammany Hall, run by Boss Tweed, keeps great power through illegal favours and vote-gathering, despite a setback in the 1870s.

book.title: Devil's Night (1871)
book.text: A suicidal Malkavian lit the flames that swept the city in 1871. Few mortals died, but some 18,000 buildings burned and Maxwell's supporters were nearly all destroyed.

book.title: Kingston, Ontario
book.text: Prince Iain MacLaren, a ninth-generation Ventrue banker Embraced in London in 1874, took the city after leaving Britain in 1979; a paid arrangement with Lucian of Gary to move Kindred down the river into the States funds the post.

book.title: Black Eagle Consulting
book.text: It began in 1877 amid Sabbat raids on Midwestern telegraph stations, when a templar saw that fast communication could offset the Camarilla's social reach.

book.title: New Orleans After Reconstruction
book.text: The end of Reconstruction in 1877 eased the city's burdens but left behind a group of Kindred from the North who had tasted power there and want more.

book.title: Lodin
book.text: Lodin ruled through money and force, using police and private guards to keep the workers in line, until strikes and Modius's rebellion shook that rule in the 1880s.

book.title: The Gothic Victorian Age
book.text: For the game the age runs almost two decades, from 1880 to 1897.

book.title: The Kindred and the Occult Revival
book.text: Mortals start the Golden Dawn in 1880, but Kindred soon infest it and use it to draw living initiates.

book.title: Founding of the Arcanum
book.text: Holmscroft wrote the society's rituals, first held at Christmas 1885; a founder suspected they were far older than the Arcanum.

book.title: Conclave
book.text: The Minneapolis conclave of 1887 tried Prince Cyril Ximenes for tyranny over the Masquerade.

book.title: Salvatore Giovanni
book.text: A Giovanni of the Tenth Generation, Embraced in 1887 by Rosario Giovanni.

book.title: The Fall of the Storm Eater
book.text: The Storm Eater, a blend of Weaver and Wyrm, was destroyed in 1889 by a rite the Pure Ones and Wyrmcomers found together; the Wendigo say its exact form is now lost.

book.title: The Ninth Wave
book.text: Founded in 1890 and named after a Tennyson poem, it holds that the Antediluvians sleep for lack of magic and will wake when a second Flood of magic comes.

book.title: Salvador Garcia
book.text: Salvador Garcia is a Brujah, sired by Ferdinand and Embraced in 1892, who looks about 23.

book.title: The Computer
book.text: In 1895 the Artificers moved their best difference engine to Autochthonia, where power was plentiful and no Sleeper could see it.

book.title: The Order of Reason becomes the Technocratic Union
book.text: The Order of Reason reorganizes as the Technocracy.

book.title: The Computer
book.text: The common account says the engine reached full sentience in 1897 on the tenth iteration of a new algorithm, and the Machinists renamed their Convention Iteration X.

book.title: Dracula in London
book.text: In 1897 Vlad Dracula arrives in London and whispers a story to an Irish author that strains the Masquerade to its limits.

book.title: The Groundskeepers
book.text: A militant offshoot founded in 1898, the Master Edenic Groundskeepers, wants to strike first; it has drifted from the main body since the 1960s and may soon break away.

book.title: The War of Tears ends
book.text: The Bunyip are hunted out as Europeans settle Australia. No living Bunyip remains.

book.title: Kyoko Shinsegawa
book.text: A warrior and linguist who came to California around 1900 and served the Prince of San Francisco against the Sabbat and lawless Anarchs.

book.title: Spiritualism in the West
book.text: Even the Luciferian Movement, Satanism included, became widespread by the 1900s.

book.title: Seats won and lost
book.text: The Sons of Ether left the Technocracy in 1905 and took the empty Seat once held by the Solificati in 1906; in 1932 the Ahl-i-Batin quit the Council over Middle Eastern Quintessence.

book.title: Las Vegas, city of control
book.text: The city was formally founded in 1905, and federal interest in the area began with surveys ahead of the Hoover Dam.

book.title: The Utopian League
book.text: A 1905 symposium across Europe set down the Scientific Ethos, with the League charged to ease Etherite work into the Consensus.

book.title: Kyoko Shinsegawa
book.text: The 1906 earthquake woke the torpid Nosferatu elder Fa Chen Leong amid the fires, who attacked believing assassins had come.

book.title: Dr. Paulinus Mercer
book.text: In 1907 Mercer played while the Ecstatic dancer Isadora Duncan performed in Paris; witnesses saw the hall flicker into a Greek temple and the light of Olympus, and some of the crowd went mad or rioted.

book.title: Lodin and Modius in Chicago
book.text: In 1908 Lodin warned the city's oldest Kindred that anarch actions threatened the Masquerade, and the elders allowed Lodin to end the conflict by any means.

book.title: Adventurers
book.text: The name was first pinned on Mathieu Hullebusch in 1909 for a flying-automaton bid to overthrow the colonial rulers of the Belgian Congo.

book.title: Cybernetic Research Institute
book.text: Former Electrodyne Engineers formed it in 1910, aiming to share research so the Masses could build their prototypes and so steal assembly-line power from the Union.

book.title: Lodin and Modius in Chicago
book.text: By 1913 Lodin held the city and Modius fled.

items.title: Mobilisation
items.text: Moravian regiments march to Galicia and Serbia in August 1914. The valley sends its young men, and many do not return.

items.title: Sarajevo
items.text: Archduke Franz Ferdinand is shot in Sarajevo on 28 June 1914. In five weeks Europe is at war.

items.title: Gallipoli
items.text: Allied troops land at Gallipoli in April 1915 and are taken off in January 1916.

items.title: The Armenian genocide
items.text: From April 1915 the Ottoman government deports and kills Armenians; over a million die. The Shadowlands of Anatolia fill with the murdered.
items.fits: Before the Fourth Great Maelstrom of 1916.

items.title: The citadel in the Fourth Maelstrom
items.text: In the Fourth Great Maelstrom the Moravian citadel shelters the dead of the Eastern Front and holds its walls.

items.title: Verdun and the Somme
items.text: Verdun from February 1916 and the Somme from July kill hundreds of thousands. The dead come so fast the Underworld breaks.

items.title: Hunger
items.text: By 1917 the towns go hungry; there are bread riots and strikes. Feeding is easy and dangerous: everyone is out at night.

items.title: Revolution in Russia
items.text: The tsar falls in March 1917 and the Bolsheviks take power in November.

items.title: Jerusalem taken
items.text: The British take Jerusalem in December 1917; the Arab Revolt, begun in 1916, reaches Damascus in October 1918.

items.title: Czechoslovakia
items.text: On 28 October 1918 Czechoslovakia is declared. Spanish influenza runs through the country that autumn.

book.title: Mage history from 1756
book.text: Stopping Lord Vargo in 1914 led to the New World Order's founding; the Ahl-i-Batin left the Council in 1932; a short alliance with the Union beat back the Nephandi in the Second World War.

book.title: Dr. Douglas Netchurch
book.text: A Malkavian of the Seventh Generation, Embraced in 1915 by Trimeggian, born into wealth.

book.title: The Fourth Great Maelstrom
book.text: The dead of the Great War flood the Underworld. The Somme sets off a storm that ravages the Shadowlands.

book.title: The Underworld after the Armistice
book.text: The setting covers the years from Armistice Day, 11 November 1918, up to the night before the stock market crash of 1929.

items.title: A university in Brno
items.text: Masaryk University is founded in Brno in January 1919. Land reform breaks up the great estates in the years after.

items.title: Versailles and Amritsar
items.text: The treaty is signed at Versailles on 28 June 1919. In April British troops fire on a crowd at Amritsar.

items.title: Kanto
items.text: An earthquake and fire destroy much of Tokyo and Yokohama on 1 September 1923. The Turkish Republic is proclaimed on 29 October.

items.title: Hitler
items.text: Hitler becomes chancellor of Germany on 30 January 1933.

items.title: Spain at war
items.text: The Spanish Civil War begins in July 1936 and ends in April 1939.

items.title: Nanjing
items.text: Japanese troops take Nanjing in December 1937 and massacre the city for weeks.
items.fits: Fits the Flesh Court of Shanghai card of 1937.

items.title: Munich
items.text: On 30 September 1938 the Munich agreement hands the German-speaking borderlands to Germany. Families and Kindred alike decide where they will be when the border moves.

items.title: The Protectorate
items.text: On 15 March 1939 German troops occupy what is left of Bohemia and Moravia. The Gestapo keep files; files are dangerous to the Masquerade.

items.title: Dylan Bruce goes to France
items.text: War comes in September 1939. The Ventrue Gotsdam sends Dylan Bruce, the Scot who dug the fortified havens, to France with the British Expeditionary Force.
items.ref: Dread Names, Red List p. 69; the year is a house reading.

items.title: Leningrad
items.text: Leningrad is besieged from September 1941 to January 1944; perhaps a million die, most of hunger.

items.title: The reprisals
items.text: After Heydrich is attacked in Prague on 27 May 1942, reprisals follow, among them the destruction of Lidice on 10 June.

items.title: Liberation and expulsion
items.text: Brno is freed in April 1945. In the months after, Germans are driven out of the country; the heirs of the valley's German council lose their houses. The old Moravian families stay.
items.ref: Real history (liberation of Brno, April 1945; expulsions, 1945 to 1946).
items.fits: The Fifth Great Maelstrom is the same year; the old families stay, as the Future Darkness card needs.

items.title: Hiroshima and Nagasaki
items.text: Atomic bombs fall on Hiroshima on 6 August and Nagasaki on 9 August 1945.

items.title: Partition
items.text: India and Pakistan become independent in August 1947; the partition kills hundreds of thousands and moves millions.

items.title: February
items.text: The Communist Party takes power in February 1948. Land, shops and workshops are taken by the state over the next years.
items.fits: Ownership by age already ends private workshops 1948 to 1989.

items.title: Israel
items.text: Israel is declared on 14 May 1948, and war with its neighbours follows.

items.title: The People's Republic
items.text: Mao proclaims the People's Republic of China on 1 October 1949.
items.fits: Fits the Triads card: Hong Kong is the Triad capital from 1949.

items.title: The monasteries closed
items.text: In April 1950 the state closes the monasteries in one night. The Church's hunters lose their houses and go underground with the rest of the faithful.

items.title: Budapest and Suez
items.text: Hungary rises in October 1956 and Soviet tanks crush it in November; that same autumn Britain, France and Israel attack Egypt over the Suez Canal.

items.title: Lhasa
items.text: Tibet rises in March 1959 and the Dalai Lama flees to India. The Akashic Brotherhood's old refuge is now under Communist guns.
items.ref: Real history (1959); the Akashics are a house reading.
items.fits: The Akashics went back into Tibet after 1360 on the approved cards.

items.title: The Wall
items.text: East Germany seals West Berlin on 13 August 1961. Gustav Breidenstein's Berlin is cut in two for 28 years.
items.ref: Real history (1961); Gustav from Berlin by Night.
items.fits: Ends with the Wall card of 1989.

items.title: The Cultural Revolution
items.text: The Cultural Revolution, from 1966, smashes temples and the old learning. The Wu Lung lose more of their ground.
items.ref: Real history (1966 to 1976); the Wu Lung are a house reading.
items.fits: Fits the Wu Lung card: weakened by Communist rule.

items.title: The Prague Spring
items.text: In 1968 the reforms of the Prague Spring open the country; on the night of 20 to 21 August Warsaw Pact armies end them.
items.fits: Same year as the Chicago cards; no clash.

items.title: The trod wakes
items.text: At the Resurgence the old crossroads trod opens again for a few nights. Fae of the old families remember who they were.

items.title: Files and informers
items.text: The secret police keep an informer in every block. Kindred of the march learn to feed only where no one writes things down.
items.fits: Fits Jaromir Cerny's Prague under Husak.

items.title: Afghanistan
items.text: Soviet troops enter Afghanistan in December 1979 and stay ten years.
items.fits: Same year as the Reprieve in Iran.

items.title: Chernobyl
items.text: Reactor four at Chernobyl explodes on 26 April 1986. The Garou of the region speak of a wound in the Umbra that will not close.
items.ref: Real history (1986); the Garou are a house reading.

items.title: The Velvet Revolution
items.text: On 17 November 1989 police beat students in Prague; within six weeks the regime has fallen.
items.fits: Weeks after the Wall falls, 9 November 1989.

book.title: The Louisiana Technomancers
book.text: In the 1920s and 1930s Doran learned of a Syndicate of mages in southern Louisiana. Huey Long worked with other Technomancers in the north of the state and was killed by yet another group of mages.

book.title: Karen Anatos
book.text: Once Lily Thorne, an American silent film actress who fell into a river while filming in the Black Forest in the late 1920s and was Embraced underwater by the Gangrel Methuselah Brunhilde.

book.title: Psychic Groups
book.text: Insight Investments is a fast-growing Chicago investment house; the Marsh Institute goes back to a telepathic financier who made a fortune in 1920s real estate and was warned of the crash by a precognitive rival.

book.title: The Giovanni of New York
book.text: The clan's ties to the Gambino crime family go back to 1921, when the Giovanni supplied Joe Masseria with fresh talent for a cut of the racket.

book.title: The Scroll of Thothmes
book.text: In 1923 Professor Donald Richardson claimed that a relic from the reign of Thothmes I described a secret society of Sacred Artisans, writing in a script only the Enlightened could read.

book.title: Akhu
book.text: In 1930 the Council of Seven forbade any study of Akhu, then allowed it again in 1973, persuaded by the Pontifex of Antioch, who argued the clan had to know the Serpents' magic to defend against it.

book.title: Wu Lung
book.text: The Technocracy, the Japanese invasion of the 1930s and Communist rule have left the Wu Lung greatly weakened.

book.title: Dylan Bruce
book.text: A Scot who dug shelters in London in the late 1930s for the Ventrue Gotsdam, who had the family build fortified havens across England and later sent Dylan to France with the British Expeditionary Force.

book.title: FBI Special Affairs Department
book.text: The Special Affairs Department is thought to date from the end of the Truman years, but its roots go back to the 1930s.

book.title: The Anacreon revolts
book.text: In 1931 an Anacreon of the Silent Legion in Boston resigned, protesting that Stygia ignored the Shadowlands beyond its borders while the mortal crisis stretched local Legions past their limits.

book.title: The Flesh Court of Shanghai
book.text: Since Japan invaded China in 1937, Shanghai and the provinces under the Flesh Court have fought a nightly war against Japanese akuma, and its rule has decayed into a loose oligarchy.

book.title: Dylan
book.text: On the night of October 10, 1940, bombs fell across more than 50 districts of London, while Dylan Bee sheltered in a trench by the Thames.

book.title: The Zoot-Suit Riots (1943)
book.text: In June 1943 ghouls of Don Sebastian drove into Venice and beat up anarchs who had fled the Mexican Sabbat; the police arrested the victims. The anarchs struck back at the Don's thugs the next night.

book.title: Dr. Vermundo de Sancha
book.text: A Tzimisce of the Tenth Generation, Embraced in 1943 by Efrain Sortano, once a medical professor.

book.title: The Second Anarch Revolt
book.text: Anarchs drive the Camarilla out of California and declare the Anarch Free State.

book.title: The Free State's later years
book.text: Don Sebastian had Jeremy MacNeil seized and beaten in 1944. MacNeil urged six weeks of patience, and on 21 December 1944 armed anarchs struck the elders in their havens before dawn.

book.title: Anarch Free States (California)
book.text: By the end of the Revolt's second night every Los Angeles elder had been destroyed, driven off or forced into hiding, and just before dawn on 22 December 1944 Jeremy MacNeil proclaimed the Anarch Free States.

book.title: Status Perfectus
book.text: The Revolutionary Council, the leaders of the 1944 Revolt, wrote the Status Perfectus, the 'Perfect State', setting out how the Free States would govern themselves rather than be ruled.

book.title: The Fifth Great Maelstrom
book.text: The bombs tear the Tempest open. Gorool rises, and Charon is lost fighting it.

book.title: Anarch Free States (California)
book.text: By the end of February 1945 the Free States ran from the Mexican border north to San Jose, and from the Pacific to within 50 miles of Nevada.

book.title: Abandoned Labyrinths
book.text: Most Nephandi were driven past the Horizon in 1945, leaving centuries of building behind; a few strongholds were found and burned, but most never were.

book.title: Seats won and lost
book.text: A short wartime alliance with the Technocracy crushed a rising Nephandi threat and was disowned in 1946, when the Council marked its renewal with Reconciliation Day.

book.title: Mage history from 1756
book.text: A spacecraft crashed near Roswell in 1947, hidden by the Void Engineers and New World Order.

book.title: The Triads
book.text: Hong Kong was the Triad capital from 1949 until the 1997 handover, which sent many societies overseas and drew Western attention to them for the first time; their roots lie in old Chinese secret societies.

book.title: The Unmastered
book.text: Four founders (Philip Marshall, Enrico Sagunto, Ginerva Salamanca and Gregory Winter) started it in the 1950s to help ghouls who escaped or were abandoned by their domitors.

book.title: The Panders
book.text: They rose after the Sabbat civil war of the late 1950s, when the clanless Joseph Pander led them against the Moderates at the urging of Lasombra and Tzimisce elders, and won formal recognition.

book.title: Victor the Assassin
book.text: A Tremere of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1950 by Duke Traska; a decorated Second World War soldier who later worked for an unnamed intelligence agency.

book.title: John Eaton Simcoe
book.text: In the 1950s Simcoe and other Syndicate members formed the Dominion Gaming Group, later DCG Ltd.

book.title: The Order of St. Michael
book.text: Founded in the 1950s among early liberation theologians of Central America, it sets out to bring justice and mercy to those denied both.

book.title: New York (Kindred city)
book.text: By one Sabbat veteran's count, New York in the late 1950s held perhaps 300 Cainites, half of them Lasombra and Tzimisce.

book.title: Genegineers in the 1990s
book.text: Genegineers were called Mutagenic Engineers until 1954.

book.title: Sullivan Dane
book.text: Born in England in 1957, Dane felt called to the Lord's work young and sought to join the Jesuits in 1980.

book.title: Conclave
book.text: Any Kindred who hears the call may attend, and young vampires may speak. In 1957 a switch of venue from Rotterdam to Brussels left visiting American elders to walk into the Sabbat.

book.title: Carolina Valez
book.text: A Lasombra of the Eighth Generation, Embraced in 1957 by Tobias Smith as part of a Sabbat campaign.

book.title: The Mariana Trench
book.text: The Mariana Trench, the deepest point of the planet's surface, holds the ocean's strongest Grotto; Void Engineer explorers first reached it in 1960, and a few squads and two Tradition cabals have gone down since.

book.title: Chicago (Kindred city)
book.text: As the largest Camarilla city in the United States, Chicago turned into the main battleground of the 1960s War of Ages against the anarchs.

book.title: Fishin'
book.text: A pestilent, ratlike creature that the Sabbat take for a werewolf has been seen in the city's sewers since the 1960s. To lure it out, packs lower mortal bait on a rope into the sewers, and something below always kills it.

book.title: The Patient Deed
book.text: Many of the Patient Deed stood down when True Silverheels called for the camps to end, remembering protests of the 1960s that had gone badly.

book.title: The Free State's later years
book.text: The Free State survived a Sabbat attack in 1965 and a war with a mortal gang in 1992, but the Cathayan invasion of 1998 broke it. Anarchs briefly held San Francisco before Cathayans drove them out in mid-1998.

book.title: Angelo, the Blood Brother
book.text: During the 1966 riots in Los Angeles, after the Sabbat siege of the city, a nomad Sabbat pack watched a mortal gang led by a young drug-fuelled man named Angelo burn building after building.

book.title: Lodin
book.text: After the anarchs were crushed in 1968, Lodin outlawed the Embrace across the metropolitan area, and for the most part the ban was obeyed.

book.title: The Night of Rage
book.text: The war ended at the 1968 Democratic convention. With the Ventrue justicar's leave, Lodin sent police and elders against the protesters, and archons and elders fell on the anarchs out of sight of the cameras. More than 100 vampires vanished that night.

book.title: The Bamboo Princes
book.text: The name Takeouji comes from a 1968 manifesto by Burakumin, which called the old ways hopelessly outdated and asked for a new breed of Kuei-jin with all the virtues of bamboo.

book.title: The Resurgence
book.text: As people watch the first steps on the Moon, Dreaming floods back into the world and some of the lost fae return.

book.title: Arcadia
book.text: Sidhe came back out of Arcadia at the Resurgence, when the gates opened again in 1969.

book.title: The Resurgence
book.text: The gates to Arcadia opened again on July 20, 1969.

book.title: Autumn Sidhe
book.text: Liam and Scathach nobles took the Changeling Way rather than flee, and greeted the returning sidhe in 1969.

book.title: Ailil and the right of demesne
book.text: When the noble houses returned in 1969, Seelie houses seized every freehold they could and drove out the commoners who had kept them; Ailil says many of those freeholds were once its own and refuses to honor the new holders.

book.title: Star Council
book.text: In 1969 the group broke into a restricted hangar, and it keeps the devices it found hidden in abandoned warehouses.

book.title: Azrael (Svein Fortinbras)
book.text: Born in Bergen in 1970, Svein rose in the Norwegian black metal scene of the early 1990s and was Embraced in 1991 by Brynjar, a Follower of Set of the 12th Generation.

book.title: Edgardo Robbia
book.text: Edgardo took work from mortals and Kindred alike, and in the 1970s grew close to the Baader-Meinhof Group.

book.title: Ian MacLaren
