book.text: After a string of financial mistakes in the 1970s, MacLaren was urged to leave and became Prince of Kingston, Ontario.

book.title: The Zaibatsu and the Elemental Dragons
book.text: Other Asian Technocratic bodies kept silent too; in the late 1970s a few Taiping Tianguo agents admitted aiding North Vietnamese forces on Syndicate orders.

book.title: Cybernetic Research Institute
book.text: The Institute was never just about computers, though its close work with the Virtual Adepts through the 1970s and 1980s led many to think so.

book.title: Vancouver, a Haven City
book.text: Several old vampires gained sway over major local businesses, including forestry firms, while Richard Daly, a rich and influential businessman who leads the Glass Walkers, became a key figure of Garou Vancouver from the early 1970s.

book.title: Highgate Cemetery
book.text: Opened in the mid-19th century, Highgate has always had ties to the supernatural, including talk of a Vampire of Highgate in the 1970s and 1980s.

book.title: Black Tooth
book.text: Black Tooth, a Simba from Zululand, gathered a pride in the ivory wars of the late 1970s and struck at all European intruders, supernatural or mundane.

book.title: Track 6A
book.text: While building Atlanta's subway in the late 1970s, MARTA crews failed again and again to blast through one stretch of granite that geologists could find nothing wrong with.

book.title: Madame Yacine
book.text: In 1974 the French Tremere won over Madame Yacine, a Malkavian practitioner living among the Algerian community of Lyon.

book.title: Colm Olliver
book.text: A Brujah of the 11th Generation, Embraced in 1974 by Fat Ciaran; ambushed and staked on a farm truck bound for London in 1976, then left in torpor three years.

book.title: Varosha
book.text: Cordoned off since the Turkish invasion of 1974, Varosha is frozen in time, its shops still hung with clothes untouched for decades.

book.title: The Batini and Iran
book.text: Training of new Qutbs began in Isfahan in October 1979.

book.title: The Reprieve of 1979
book.text: In 1979 the Shah's government fell and Technocratic agents were driven out of Iran, a turn the Batini call the Reprieve.

book.title: Maria DiMatto
book.text: DiMatto, child of a Giovanni cousin, was Embraced in 1980 after a youthful fascination with the darker side of the family.

book.title: Atlantic City
book.text: Few Restless gathered in Atlantic City until gambling was made legal there in 1980; before that its dead were mostly Enfants and old wraiths bound to happier summers, ignored by Hierarchy and Heretic alike.

book.title: Sullivan Dane
book.text: In 1982 Dane destroyed a neonate in Washington, D.C., and in that moment was flooded with names, faces and scenes, sure of a calling to hunt vampires.

book.title: The Russian Silence
book.text: In 1985 the Council sought a normal footing with the Camarilla against unnamed threats; in 1990 all contact stopped, then all contact with any Kindred in Russia, and Tremere spying there failed.

book.title: The Mexico City earthquake of 1985
book.text: The quake of 19 September 1985 damaged over 4,000 buildings and killed more than 9,000 people.

book.title: Lodin
book.text: In 1986, in return for Annabelle's support against the anarch leader Maldavis, Lodin had to let Annabelle make two childer and to attend the primogen in Elysium on the first Monday of every month.

book.title: Chicago primogen
book.text: Procet, a member of the council, vanished in the Thanksgiving Massacre of 1986, when Lodin's mortal servants staked anarchs in their havens by day.

book.title: The House of Storms
book.text: Its resident, Kathryn Green, made a fortune in the 1987 stock market crash by buying while others sold.

book.title: Baba Yaga and the Fall of the Wall
book.text: Even Gustav was caught off guard when the crossing points opened on November 9, 1989; hoping to win back lost ground, the prince let the Wall come down from June 13, 1990.

book.title: Meixiu
book.text: A Malkavian of the 10th Generation, Embraced in 1989 by Colin McAllister; each night the delusion of being the Black Dragon Princess, heir of the Yellow Emperor, grows stronger.

book.title: Jaromir Cerny
book.text: Old Clan Tzimisce of the 8th Generation, Embraced in 1989 by Janek Ritka; dissident parents were arrested in Prague under Gustav Husak.

name: Modern and the Time of Judgment

items.title: The end of the Soviet Union
items.text: The Soviet Union ends on 26 December 1991.
items.fits: The mortal side of the Shadow Curtain; supernatural Russia stays hidden. Classic timeline only; the Future Darkness branch keeps its own approved history from 1990.

items.title: The Gulf War
items.text: A coalition drives Iraq out of Kuwait in January and February 1991.
items.fits: No clash. Classic timeline only; the Future Darkness branch keeps its own approved history from 1990.

items.title: Konietzko and the Balkan wars
items.text: Yugoslavia breaks apart in war from 1991; Sarajevo is besieged from 1992 to 1996, and Srebrenica falls in July 1995. Margrave Konietzko directs the Garou against the Wyrm's forces in Serbia from the Sept of the Night Sky.
items.ref: Real history (1991 to 1995); Konietzko from Tribe Novel: Silent Striders & Black Furies p. 32; the timing is a house reading.
items.fits: No clash. Classic timeline only; the Future Darkness branch keeps its own approved history from 1990.

items.title: The Czech Republic
items.text: On 1 January 1993 Czechoslovakia splits in two. Moravia is in the Czech Republic.
items.fits: No clash. Classic timeline only; the Future Darkness branch keeps its own approved history from 1990.

items.title: The show mine
items.text: The valley's Adit is reopened as a show mine for visitors. Guides tell of ghost miners; some of the stories are true.

items.title: Kobe
items.text: An earthquake kills over six thousand people in Kobe on 17 January 1995.
items.fits: No clash. Classic timeline only; the Future Darkness branch keeps its own approved history from 1990.

items.title: The great flood
items.text: In July 1997 the Morava and Oder flood much of Moravia. Towns go under, and the Shadowlands shift.
items.fits: No clash. Classic timeline only; the Future Darkness branch keeps its own approved history from 1990.

items.title: The handover
items.text: Hong Kong goes back to China on 1 July 1997.
items.fits: The same year the Quincunx moves to take Hong Kong from the Kin-jin; Anguo Chun's line on Kin-jin fits after it. Classic timeline only; the Future Darkness branch keeps its own approved history from 1990.

items.title: Refuge in the citadel
items.text: When the Sixth Great Maelstrom breaks, the Moravian citadel takes in wraiths from across the east. It is the strongest the Hierarchy holds there.
items.fits: The Sixth Great Maelstrom, 1999; leads into the Future Darkness cards where Moravia is the Hierarchy's last fortress.

items.title: NATO
items.text: The Czech Republic joins NATO on 12 March 1999.

items.title: Kosovo
items.text: NATO bombs Yugoslavia from March to June 1999 over Kosovo.
items.fits: Same year as the Week of Nightmares and the Reckoning. Classic timeline only; the Future Darkness branch keeps its own approved history from 1990.

items.title: The museum looted
items.text: The United States invades Iraq in March 2003; in April the Baghdad museum is looted. Relics older than any mummy go missing.
items.ref: Real history (2003); the relics are a house reading.
items.fits: No clash. Classic timeline only; the Future Darkness branch keeps its own approved history from 1990.

items.title: Into the European Union
items.text: The Czech Republic joins the European Union on 1 May 2004.
items.fits: The Time of Judgment year. Stands on its own because it is mundane; whatever the Storyteller chooses for the endings, the treaty is signed.

items.title: Sichuan
items.text: An earthquake in Sichuan kills about seventy thousand people on 12 May 2008.
items.fits: After the Time of Judgment year: stands only when the Storyteller skips the endings. Classic timeline only; the Future Darkness branch keeps its own approved history from 1990.

book.title: The Russian Silence
book.text: With Soviet money gone, Anarchs in Latin America and Africa lost heavily through the 1990s.

book.title: Baba Yaga and the Fall of the Wall
book.text: Baba Yaga stirred from torpor in 1990 and set out to bring the eastern lands back under the Nosferatu elder's control.

book.title: The Locksmiths
book.text: The Locksmiths began in the late 1990s, founded by a Glass Walker called only Strangelove, as a network for Glass Walker Kinfolk.

book.title: The Shadow Curtain
book.text: When the Baba Yaga rose and the Shadow Curtain fell in the early 1990s, supernatural Russia disappeared behind an invisible barrier.

book.title: The Succubus Club
book.text: The first club opened in Chicago in the early 1990s, where Kindred fed on mortals drawn to the vampire scene; tonight it is a nomadic party moving across North America.

book.title: The Russian Silence
book.text: From 1991 four archon teams went in, the last with a former Justicar, and none returned; the Camarilla now leaves Russia alone and hopes whatever is there stays put.

book.title: Lula Birch
book.text: A Gangrel antitribu of the Twelfth Generation, Embraced in 1991 by Pedro Diaz, raised in Arkansas farm country.

book.title: Lodin's Boardroom
book.text: In 1993 Prince Lodin called a Blood Hunt on the werewolves and died in the Lupine rampage, along with half the city's Kindred.

book.title: The werewolf war of 1993
book.text: On a moonlit night in 1993, werewolves struck the heart of the city, aiming at the Succubus Club. Lodin called a Blood Hunt on the Lupines.

book.title: Ayisha Jocastian
book.text: A letter of Ayisha's travels, on Giovanni and Setite influence, appeared in the 1993 edition of the ancient Noddist scripture compiled by Aristotle de Laurent and Beckett.

book.title: Conclave
book.text: Conclaves meet for grave matters, trials of mighty Kindred or the removal of corrupt princes, and they often rule on the Traditions. The 1994 conclave took up the Internet and the Masquerade.

book.title: The Montreal archdiocese
book.text: In 1994 Ezekiel, childe of Sangris, returned at the head of a Black Hand pack to claim the seat, and the Shepherds put forward the former inquisitor Alfred Benezri. Each of the city's covens has lined up behind one of the three.

book.title: Pentex’s corporate history
book.text: Its later directors include Harold Zettler and Executive Vice President Peter Culliford, whose combined experience is said to span more than a thousand years; Culliford reorganised the Board into its present subdivisions in 1994.

book.title: ShreckNet
book.text: ShreckNet began as a joke name for secret Nosferatu hubs on the early military network; privatisation in 1995 and the boom in hubs shrank it to a vampire-only net across about thirty cities.

book.title: The fall of the College on Mus
book.text: In August 1995 a Technocratic fleet attacked the Chantry; a third force of Umbrood, wormlike beasts and Nephandi then struck both sides and took the College.

book.title: The Martian Penumbra
book.text: Two Tradition settlements stand where seven canals meet, the Trivium Charontis: the terraformed grounds of Doissetep, whose great house sits in an overlap zone with the Shade Realm of Forces, and a Sons of Ether camp nicknamed Bradbury, set up with the Deacons' leave in summer 1996.

book.title: The fall of Doissetep
book.text: The Hermetic stronghold destroys itself. The Digital Web crashes in the Great Whiteout.

book.title: Bone Flowers in Hong Kong
book.text: That uneasy peace fell apart in 1997, when the Quincunx resolved to seize Hong Kong from the Kin-jin by force.

book.title: The Pogrom
book.text: In 1997 a cabal tried to bring down a Horizon Construct, setting off days of slaughter on the Front Lines.

book.title: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe
book.text: Ratkin Tunnel Runners riddled the Shadow Curtain over Asia with boltholes, and when it fell in late 1998 the local wererats claimed the credit.

book.title: The Breaking
book.text: Until late 1998 every Assamite carried the Tremere curse: vampire blood harmed them and gave no nourishment, and attempted diablerie burned them with no gain.

book.title: Baba Yaga
book.text: In 1998 Lupines slew Baba Yaga. The Shadow Curtain fell, and Russian Nosferatu now hide as autarkis between the Camarilla to the west and Cathayans eager for the old domains to the east.

book.title: Justicars
book.text: Since the Gangrel left the sect, there has been no Gangrel justicar; Xaviar was the last. By the 1998 meeting most of the justicars were new appointees.

book.title: The death of the Baba Yaga
book.text: Through 1998 the Garou dismantled the Baba Yaga’s power piece by piece, and that obsession with the werewolves may have left the sorceress open to vampire foes.

book.title: The Fallen escape the Abyss
book.text: Fallen angels slip out of their prison and take the bodies of the dying.

book.title: The Reckoning
book.text: The first of the imbued see the world as it is. From now on hunters follow Hunter: The Reckoning.

book.title: The Sixth Great Maelstrom
book.text: The greatest storm of all scours the Underworld. In its chaos the Abyss cracks and the mummies' souls are torn loose.

book.title: The Avatar Storm
book.text: A storm in the spirit world flays the souls of mages who try to cross the Gauntlet.

book.title: The Week of Nightmares
book.text: A week of mass nightmares and visions as something ancient wakes and rampages across India and Bangladesh.

book.title: ShreckNet
book.text: After a 1999 scare over a bulletin board for monster hunters, the Camarilla set up a task force to watch the Internet; it now uses scores of vampires and thousands of servants and is still too small.

book.title: The naraka
book.text: In the summer of 1999 the Dreaming around Bangladesh was almost wiped out by fire; the naraka emerged into the Autumn World from that wasteland, the first thing they saw being Kali the destroyer, whom they took as mother.

book.title: Research & Execution
book.text: R&E repairs gear and vessels and runs labs; 32.7% of its people stay home, down from about 55% before 1999.

book.title: The Dimensional Anomaly
book.text: The Anomaly struck at the end of June 1999, tearing across the Spatial Horizon like a hurricane with reality at its eye.

book.title: Vitel and Garlotte
book.text: Marcus Vitel became prince of Washington some thirty years before 1999, when the previous prince, Marissa of Clan Tremere, met an end; Garlotte, prince of nearby Baltimore, has been a rival ever since and took Vitel in after Washington fell.

book.title: The generals of the 1999 Sabbat war
book.text: The Sabbat offensive begun in mid-June 1999 took Atlanta, Washington and most cities between; three archbishops led it: Sascha Vykos (newly made archbishop in Washington), Borges (of Miami) and Francisco Polonia (of New York).

book.title: The strike on Monçada
book.text: In September 1999 Lucita went to Madrid, where the Cardinal Monçada kept a haven beneath the church of San Nicolás de las Servitas, while the Assamite Fatima gathered word of its defences.

book.title: The Cyber Dogs
book.text: At the end of 1999, Elizabeth Genereader of the Random Interrupts told the tribe by video link that the Cyber Dogs had experimented on unwilling lupus Garou.

book.title: ShreckNet
book.text: After a Malkavian blogger's breach in 2000 many elders banned it, which in effect gave the Internet to the Anarchs and angered young Kindred of every sect.

book.title: The Eldest and the du'at
book.text: The du'at was the council of the three caste heads: the Caliph of the warriors, the Vizier of the viziers and the Amr of the sorcerers. Alamut's records date it to around 2000 BC.

book.title: The Assamite Schism
book.text: Schismatics first appeared publicly in early 2000. They read Haqim's Law of Judgement with moderation and call the slaughter of all other vampires genocide.

book.title: The Dimensional Anomaly
book.text: It began to ease by New Year's Day 2000 and lessened again by autumn 2000, yet it never fully ended.

book.title: Fangster
book.text: In 2001 a coterie of Tremere defectors brought Technomancy lore to the Free States and, backed by the Red Question, released free programs with ritual effects built in, usable without any knowledge of Thaumaturgy.

book.title: The Evanescence
book.text: The Evanescence is dated to around September 11, 2001.

book.title: The Time of Judgment
book.text: The end the lines foretold. Each line's ending is the Storyteller's to choose, or to skip.

book.title: The Bhuvar
book.text: Disasters in the living world of India, such as the 2004 tsunami and the yearly monsoon floods, echo as dangers in the Bhuvar, the realm of the dead beside it.
